head_commit.message:
[OPIK-8274] [BE] perf: stream feedback score bulk inserts via the ClickHouse v2 client (#8405)

* [OPIK-8274] [BE] perf: stream feedback score bulk inserts via the ClickHouse v2 client

The ClickHouse R2DBC driver resolves every bind(name, value) with a linear scan
over the statement's parameter names, so a bulk insert that renders one
placeholder per column per row binds in O(n^2). Feedback scores carry 10
row-indexed names per row on the authored table, and the batch is not capped the
way the other bulk endpoints are: ExperimentItemBulkIngestionService accumulates
up to 100 scores per record over up to 1000 records into a single call.

JsonEachRowBulkInsert factors out the plumbing ExperimentAggregatesDAOImpl
already uses for experiment_item_aggregates: rows are serialized to JSONEachRow
and streamed through the ClickHouse Java client v2 — one HTTP body, compressed
once by the client, parsed server-side. Rows are written straight into the
client's output stream one at a time, so peak memory is a single row, and the
writer re-serializes from the source collection on each invocation so the
client's own retry replays an identical body.

Both paths stay in the image behind bulkInsert.v2ClientEnabled, defaulting to
false so an upgrade does not change the write path and CI keeps covering R2DBC.
Keeping both is deliberate for the A/B: one image produces both arms.

Cell-level parity: every value comes from the same helper the R2DBC binder uses;
created_at/last_updated_at stay absent so their column DEFAULTs stamp them
server-side (last_updated_at is the ReplacingMergeTree version, so a zero there
would make every later score for the same key lose to the original row); value
is written as a quoted plain string into Decimal(18, 9); an absent
source_queue_id is "" for the FixedString(36) with no DEFAULT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] split the bulk insert across pools: serialize on boundedElastic, HTTP on chc-operation

A probe against a real ClickHouse showed the two halves were on the wrong pools.
The DataStreamWriter callback IS the HTTP body pump, so serializing inside it put
every row's Jackson work on the client's chc-operation pool — an unbounded
Executors.newCachedThreadPool — while the boundedElastic thread this Mono ran on
did nothing but park on Future.get():

    submit-thread=boundedElastic-10   writer-thread=chc-operation-1

Two threads per insert, and the CPU-bound half on the pool with no bound. Now the
batch is rendered to a buffer on boundedElastic (bounded at 10 x cores) and the
finished buffer is handed to the client, whose future is consumed with
Mono.fromFuture so no thread of ours waits on it:

    serialize-thread=boundedElastic-2   http-thread=chc-operation-2

ByteArrayOutputStream#writeTo passes the backing array to the client without
copying it again, and makes the writer replayable for free: the client's onRetry
re-invokes it and gets identical bytes.

Mono.fromFuture unwraps the future's CompletionException, so the cause reaching
RetryUtils.handleConnectionError is still the client's own exception and the
manual ExecutionException unwrapping is no longer needed.

Rows are framed with BufferedWriter#newLine(). That writes System.lineSeparator()
rather than a fixed '\n'; ClickHouse treats the \r of a Windows \r\n as inter-row
whitespace, and the backend runs on Linux where the two are the same byte. The
ordering this forces is the subtle part: rows go through the generator's buffer
while the separator goes straight to the writer, so FLUSH_AFTER_WRITE_VALUE stays
enabled to push each row out before its terminator, and FLUSH_PASSED_TO_STREAM is
disabled so that flush does not also drain the BufferedWriter.

The trade is holding the batch in memory instead of streaming a row at a time.
For feedback scores that is a large count of small rows rather than the reverse,
and it buys the bound on the half whose cost scales with the batch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] flush the writer explicitly once the batch is rendered

BufferedWriter.close() already flushed it, so this changes no bytes — the unit
tests assert the payload exactly and are unchanged. But FLUSH_PASSED_TO_STREAM is
disabled, so nothing before the close pushes the writer into the byte buffer, and
the payload's completeness rested on try-with-resources alone. Making it explicit
keeps that guarantee local to the method rather than a consequence of two Jackson
feature flags and a close.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] review: validate before the branch, cover the authorless path

Three findings from review, two of them real.

1. A null score value NPE'd on the v2 path. bindParameters rejects it per item
   with a named IllegalArgumentException -- its comment records that the NPE it
   replaced took the whole batch, and every other score in it, down. toJsonRow
   bypassed that and reached score.value().toPlainString(). The check now runs in
   insertFeedbackScores ahead of the path branch, which is the single funnel all
   three public entry points reach, so both writers reject the same input and the
   R2DBC path keeps the identical message. Removed from bindParameters rather
   than duplicated.

2. The authorless branch of toJsonRow had no coverage. Both integration tests go
   over HTTP, where FeedbackScoreService#getAuthor always supplies an author, so
   only authored_feedback_scores was exercised -- a mis-selected table or a
   wrongly emitted author/source_queue_id would have passed the suite. Added a
   DAO-seam test that asserts the row lands in feedback_scores, that nothing
   leaked into authored_feedback_scores, and that value/reason/source survive.
   Plus one pinning the rejection in (1) with v2 selected.

3. Not a code change: the retry comment claimed RetryUtils.handleConnectionError
   governs failures here. It does wrap this path via
   ExperimentItemBulkIngestionService and the resource layer, but it matches
   SocketException subclasses, and the v2 client fails transport drops with
   Apache HC's NoHttpResponseException, which is not one. So a dropped response
   is retried on R2DBC and not on v2. That gap belongs to the v2 client rather
   than this class -- the DatasetItemVersionDAO queries already on it have it
   too -- so the comment now states it instead of implying coverage, and
   widening the filter goes with the other v2-client settings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] review: overflow-safe, capped initial buffer sizing

items.size() * ESTIMATED_ROW_BYTES is int arithmetic and overflows past ~8.4M
rows, reaching ByteArrayOutputStream as a negative capacity and failing the batch
with "Negative initial size" rather than writing it. Done in long now, and capped
at 8MB so a wrong per-row guess costs a few doublings instead of a large eager
allocation the batch may never need.

Not reachable today -- the feedback score endpoints cap a batch at 1000 items
(@Size on FeedbackScoreBatchContainer) and ExperimentItemBulkUpload caps the whole
request at 4MB -- but the sizing should not depend on a caller-side limit to stay
in range.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] drop the buffer sizing hint and its cap

Reverts the sizing half of f9020422cc. Both constants are gone; the buffer is
just new ByteArrayOutputStream().

The overflow that commit fixed was real but was fixed by the long arithmetic, not
by the cap -- the cap was bundled in and never load-bearing. And the cap could not
fire for any caller: it needed >32k items in one batch, while
FeedbackScoreBatchContainer caps a batch at 1000 items and ExperimentItemBulkUpload
caps the whole request at 4MB. Those are the same bounds used to answer the
"unbounded heap" review finding, so guarding past them contradicted that argument.

With no multiply there is nothing left to overflow, which is a better outcome than
computing a hint carefully and then clamping it. The remaining cost is
ByteArrayOutputStream doubling from 32 bytes, which against a payload the
endpoints cap in the low MB is a few hundred KB of copying, and invisible next to
the insert it precedes.

Making it configurable was the alternative and would have been worse: a
BulkInsertConfig field, config.yml and config-test.yml entries, and an
operator-facing setting, all for an allocation hint nobody can usefully tune.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] say why the payload buffer sits outside the try-with-resources

Two other ByteArrayOutputStream uses in the backend (CsvDatasetExportProcessor,
OptimizationLogSyncService) do manage it as a resource, so this one reads as an
oversight without a reason attached. It is not the same shape: both of those copy
out with toByteArray() inside the block and let the buffer die there, while this
one is handed to the client as writeTo and read on the chc-operation thread after
the method returns.

Matching them would mean toByteArray(), i.e. a full copy of the payload -- the
copy writeTo exists to avoid. Wrapping it while still returning it would be safe,
since ByteArrayOutputStream.close() is a documented no-op, but would declare a
managed resource and then use it after close.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] move toJsonRow into a package-private FeedbackScoreJsonRowMapper

FeedbackScoreDAOImpl was carrying the JSONEachRow row construction inline. Moved
to FeedbackScoreJsonRowMapper, alongside the other *Mapper classes in this
package; the DAO loses 44 lines and keeps only the path selection and the two
writers.

getValueOrDefault moved with it rather than being duplicated. It is called by
bindParameters as well as toJsonRow, and "every value comes from the same helper
the R2DBC binder uses" is the parity property the toggle rests on -- two copies
could drift on how an absent value is normalized and produce different cells for
the same input. There is still exactly one; the binder static-imports it.

No @UtilityClass: Lombok makes the members static during annotation processing,
but javac resolves `import static` before that runs, so the binder's import
cannot see the method and the build fails. Explicit static with a private
constructor, which is what DatasetItemResultMapper does.

Behaviour unchanged. Unit 11/0, BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 4/0, and
MultiValueFeedbackScoresE2ETest 17/0 on the R2DBC path, which is the one that
exercises the relocated helper through bindParameters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] centralize the trim-to-empty normalization on StringUtils

baz flagged getValueOrDefault as misnamed: it takes no default, it trims and maps
null/blank to "". Renaming it was the suggestion; deleting it is better, because
the body is character-for-character StringUtils.trimToEmpty -- null -> "",
"  " -> "", " x " -> "x" -- and that idiom is already used in OpenTelemetryMapper
and GoogleProviderResolver.

Both copies are gone: the one this PR had relocated into
FeedbackScoreJsonRowMapper, and the pre-existing identical private copy in
AssertionResultDAO. The name no longer needs improving and there is nothing left
to keep in sync; grep for getValueOrDefault across the backend now returns
nothing.

AssertionResultDAO is outside this PR's feedback-score scope, but leaving the
duplicate would have left the same finding live in a file this PR does not touch,
with no reviewer attached to it.

Behaviour unchanged. Unit 11/0, BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 4/0,
MultiValueFeedbackScoresE2ETest 17/0 (R2DBC, exercises the binder), and
AssertionResultsResourceTest 4/0 for the second file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] normalize the batch-invariant author once, not per row

author is one value for the whole batch, but both writers ran trimToEmpty on it
inside their per-row loop. Hoisted in bindParameters and in insertJsonEachRow.

null stays distinct from "": it is null, not empty, that selects the unauthored
table and drops the author/source_queue_id columns with it, so the hoisted value
is left null rather than flattened. The mapper's parameter is renamed to
normalizedAuthor and its javadoc states the contract, rather than leaving "the
caller already trimmed this" implicit.

The saving is negligible and the reason to take it is that it costs nothing:
String.trim() returns this after checking two characters when there is no
surrounding whitespace, so this was microseconds across a 100k batch.

Unit 11/0, BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 4/0, MultiValueFeedbackScoresE2ETest
17/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] manage the JsonGenerator as a resource, not a manual close

generator.close() was the last statement of the try block, so a row that failed
to serialize -- a throwing rowMapper, or Jackson rejecting a value -- skipped it
entirely and left the generator's char buffer out of Jackson's recycler. The
writer was always safe because try-with-resources owned it; the generator was
not.

Declared after the writer so it closes first: the generator drains into the
writer, then the writer into payload. That is the same order the manual close
produced on the happy path, and now it also holds when the loop throws.

This drops the explicit writer.flush(). It sat before generator.close() in the
new ordering, which is premature -- it would flush a writer the generator has not
drained into yet. Completeness now rests on try-with-resources' close order
rather than on a manual call, which is the stronger guarantee of the two since it
survives the exception path as well.

Byte-for-byte identical output: the unit tests assert the payload exactly and are
unchanged. 11/0, and BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 4/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] review: Andres' feedback across the mapper, the helper and the tests

Main code:
- stripToEmpty over trimToEmpty, in all three files. Not a no-op: strip() cuts
  Unicode whitespace where trim() cuts only <= U+0020, so a reason padded with
  U+2002 or U+3000 is now altered where it was not. Rare, and applies to the
  R2DBC path too since the helper is shared -- called out on the review thread.
- Table names extracted to constants.
- @UtilityClass on the mapper. It failed before only because getValueOrDefault
  was static-imported from it; that helper is gone, so the blocker went too.
- Nullable argument moved last in toJsonRow, so the signature can be overloaded.
- SentinelTranslation.nullToEmptyUuid replaces the inline Optional dance.
- ObjectMapper injected instead of JsonUtils.getMapper(), which is a static field
  the app replaces at startup and is on its way out. Guicey binds the Dropwizard
  mapper, which OpikApplication configures with NON_NULL and snake_case -- the
  properties this class depends on.
- CollectionUtils.isEmpty so null is handled alongside empty.

toPlainString: checked rather than assumed. The R2DBC binder uses toString(),
which switches to scientific notation, so an ordinary 0.0000001 goes out as
"1E-7". Against a real ClickHouse both notations parse to the same
Decimal(18, 9), through JSONEachRow and through FORMAT Values, as do 1E+3 and
-1E-7. The wire bytes differ from the R2DBC path; the stored cell does not, and
nothing already stored is affected.

Tests:
- Both round-trip cases are now black box, asserting whole FeedbackScore objects
  through usingRecursiveFieldByFieldElementComparatorIgnoringFields with the
  shared TraceAssertions.IGNORED_FIELDS_SCORES. That constant ignores
  valueByAuthor and sourceQueueId, which are two of the columns this path writes,
  so those two are asserted separately with a note saying why.
- Server-stamped timestamps now assert through the API, which exposes them.
- Random values throughout; expected bodies are built from the random inputs.
- Checked exceptions bubble instead of being wrapped in AssertionError.
- Dropped the two unit cases the integration test already covers end to end
  (UTF-8, newline escaping): 11 -> 9.

Two direct-access exceptions remain, each justified in the test: the raw no-FINAL
count(), because reads collapse duplicates and nothing else sees a double write;
and the two DAO-seam tests, because getAuthor means no HTTP request reaches the
authorless branch and bean validation rejects a null value long before the DAO.

Unit 9/0, BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 4/0, MultiValueFeedbackScoresE2ETest
17/0, AssertionResultsResourceTest 4/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] cover the blank-author case on the authored table

baz flagged that only null author is covered. Checked the contract first rather
than assuming a gap meant a bug: StringTemplate's <if(author)> is true for "" and
for whitespace, so the R2DBC template picks authored_feedback_scores for a blank
author exactly as this path's author != null does. The two writers agree; what
was missing was the test, not the behaviour.

Parameterized over "" and "   ": both stay on the authored table, the author
column normalizes to "", and nothing lands in feedback_scores. Reachable because
FeedbackScoreService#getAuthor returns Optional.of(userName) with no blank
filter, so an empty context username would arrive here as "" rather than null.

BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 6/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] drop the stress harness from the branch

It was never meant to be committed and was swept in by a broad `git add` on the
test tree in bb92d5f5fa. It asserts nothing -- it prints timings -- so in CI it
would be a test that cannot fail, and its 50k R2DBC case holds the job for ~9
minutes. Local-only tool.

Removed from the branch; the file stays untracked in the working copy for
re-running the A/B.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] name the count variables for what they hold

unauthored/authored/storedRows hold count() results but read like categories or
collections. Renamed to unauthoredCount/authoredCount/storedRowCount so the
isZero() and isEqualTo(size) assertions say what they mean. All three renamed,
not just the one flagged, since they had the same problem.

BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 6/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [OPIK-8274] drop the raw row-count assertion from the batch test

baz flagged it as merge-timing dependent. Checking the DDL, the premise does not
hold for the healthy path: ORDER BY is
(workspace_id, project_id, entity_type, entity_id, author, name) and the test
writes three distinct names, so the rows have distinct sorting keys and a
ReplacingMergeTree merge never collapses them. The assertion could not fail
spuriously.

It is the unhealthy path that was weak, which is worse. The failure this
assertion existed to catch -- a writer emitting every row twice -- produces
duplicate-key versions, and those a merge can collapse before the read. So it
could silently pass on a real double write, which is the opposite of what I told
the black-box thread it was buying.

Removed rather than reinforced: writesOneNewlineDelimitedRowPerItem already
asserts the exact body bytes, one JSON row per item, deterministically and at the
source. The weaker echo of it here was the last direct-SQL use in this test, so
the batch case is now fully black box.

BulkInsertV2ClientIntegrationTest 6/0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
